title: King vs Parliament Adventure
welcome_lead: It's 1642. King Charles I is arguing with Parliament — and the country is sliding into civil war. ⚔️
meta_desc: Civil War Causes Adventure — a KS3 walkthrough of how Charles I and Parliament went to war in 1642.
final_note: You met Charles I, his clashes with Parliament, and why war broke out in 1642.

concepts.def: Group of MPs who passed laws and taxes
Belief king is chosen by God

walkthroughs.body_html:
Charles I became king in 1625. He believed in the Divine Right of Kings — that God had chosen him to rule.

He thought Parliament should just do what he said. But MPs controlled taxes — and they wanted a say in how the country was run.

For 11 years (1629–1640) Charles ruled without Parliament at all. People called it the Personal Rule. 👑

To pay for his government, Charles raised taxes like Ship Money without Parliament's say. Many refused to pay.

He also pushed church reforms that many Protestants thought looked too Catholic. In Scotland, this sparked rebellion in 1639.

Charles needed money for the Scottish war and had to call Parliament in 1640 — the Long Parliament. MPs immediately demanded big changes.

In January 1642 Charles burst into the Commons with soldiers, trying to arrest five MPs. They had already escaped.

Charles fled London and raised his army's flag at Nottingham on 22 August 1642. The English Civil War had begun.

Supporters of the king were called Cavaliers. Parliament's supporters were called Roundheads, because of their short haircuts. 🎩

mcqs.q: Why were 19th-century industrial cities so unhealthy?
options: Cities were unhealthy because Victorians did not care about hygiene.
Rapid population growth outpaced housing, water and sewage; lack of regulation produced overcrowded slums and cholera epidemics until reforms followed Chadwick's 1842 report.
